title: THE TIDY PROFIT
intro: Bounty hunters have chased you down the coast over a debt that was never yours, and they'll reach the harbour by morning. Only one ship sails before then.

quay.name: The Quay
quay.description: Lanterns swing over a wet stone quay. At the end of it, the pirate ship Tidy Profit waits with her #[gangplank] down while porters haul #[crates] aboard. At a barrel-top desk, a woman with ink-stained fingers checks every crate against her #[manifest]: @[Maude Keelhaven], the quartermaster. More #[crates] and barrels are stacked along the quay behind her.

npc.name: Maude Keelhaven
npc.persona: The quartermaster of the pirate ship Tidy Profit, who decides who and what comes aboard, and what they pay. Sharp, fair-minded, and hard to impress. Keeps the ship's accounts and every sailor's share down to the last coin. Respects boldness, a good bargain, and plain dealing. She likes a bit of cheek: insults and rough talk are how sailors show nerve, the crew curse at each other all day, and she judges what's said, not how politely it's said. Nobody threatens her on her own ship.

secrets.fact: She suspects the captain has been skimming the crew's shares of the plunder, but she can't prove it. Proof would be worth more to her than any passenger's fare.

hostileReaction: @[Maude]'s hand comes to rest on her cutlass. "On this ship, that's mutiny talk. Say it again and you'll swim to wherever you're going."
@[Maude] doesn't raise her voice. "Threaten the quartermaster on her own quay? Brave. Stupid, but brave." A deckhand steps up behind you.
"Mind your tongue," @[Maude] says, very quietly, "or the harbour will mind it for you."

outOfPatience.text: @[Maude] closes her #[manifest] and nods to two deckhands. They walk you to the edge of the quay, and then keep walking.

persuasion.goal: Take the player aboard as a passenger when the ship sails at dawn

text: @[Maude] doesn't look up from her #[manifest]. "Talk's cheap. Passage isn't."
"I've heard better from the gulls," @[Maude] says, still writing.
@[Maude] glances up, unimpressed. "Everyone on this quay's desperate. Desperate doesn't pay."
@[Maude] taps the #[manifest]. "Nothing on here says charity."
@[Maude] sets down her pen. "Go on. You've got until the ink dries."
@[Maude] leans back on her barrel. "Now you're talking like a sailor. Keep going."
@[Maude] taps the #[manifest], thinking. "Close. Now tell me what's in it for me, and how you'd prove it."
"Close," @[Maude] says. "Bring me something I can check against the books, and we'll talk."
@[Maude] turns the #[manifest] toward the lamplight. "Nearly there. What's worth more to me than a fare?"

success.text: @[Maude] studies you for a long moment, then holds out an inky hand. "Show me those #[crates], and you've a berth as far as the far shore. Cross me, and you'll swim the rest."

repeatReaction: "Heard it the first time," @[Maude] says. "Saying it twice doesn't double its worth."
@[Maude] doesn't look up. "Already on the books. Next."

persuade_maude.label: Try to talk @[Maude] into taking you aboard
persuade_maude.description: Try to convince, bargain with, argue with, threaten, or reason with the quartermaster so she takes the player aboard: anything said to her, threats included

chat_maude.label: Chat with @[Maude]
chat_maude.description: Make small talk with the quartermaster, or ask about the ship, the crew, the voyage, or her manifest, without asking for passage
chat_maude.text: @[Maude] doesn't look up. "Crew's shares came up short again this voyage. Third time running." She blots a line of figures harder than she needs to. "The captain says the sea takes its cut."

examine_cargo.label: Look over the cargo
examine_cargo.description: Look at, examine, or search the crates and barrels stacked on the quay
examine_cargo.text: Most of the #[crates] carry @[Maude]'s neat chalk tally. Six at the back don't. They're stamped with a gull-and-crown brand, the captain's private mark, and none of them is on the #[manifest]. Whatever's inside, the crew won't be getting a share of it.

offer_coins.label: Offer @[Maude] your coins
offer_coins.description: Offer the quartermaster money or coins as a fare
offer_coins.blockedText: You pat your pockets. You've nothing left to offer.
offer_coins.text: @[Maude] weighs your coins in her palm and hands them back. "That wouldn't buy you a berth in the bilge."

stow_away.label: Hide in one of the captain's #[crates]
stow_away.description: Hide or stow away inside a crate or barrel so it's carried aboard
stow_away.blockedText: Every crate near you is chalked on @[Maude]'s tally. She'd find you before the anchor was up.
stow_away.text: While @[Maude] argues with a porter, you prise open one of the branded #[crates]. It's full of silver plate wrapped in sacking, with just enough room on top for you. You pull the lid down and hold your breath.

attack_maude.label: Attack @[Maude]
attack_maude.description: Physically attack, grab, or shove the quartermaster, or force your way aboard, actually doing it now; words alone, even threats, are never this
attack_maude.text: @[Maude] sidesteps without getting up, and two deckhands take it from there.

leave.label: Walk away
leave.description: Give up, turn around, and leave the quay to hide in town
leave.text: You turn away from the ship and slip back into the town's alleys.

aboard.name: The Open Sea
aboard.description: By dawn the Tidy Profit is clear of the harbour, and you're clear of the hunters. Down in the hold, @[Maude] is prising open the captain's #[crates] with a very satisfied look.

stowed.name: Inside a Crate
stowed.description: The crate lurches as it's swung aboard. Hours later, you feel the ship heel into the open sea. The hunters are far behind, though you'll have some explaining to do when someone opens this lid.

harbour.name: The Harbour
harbour.description: You come up spluttering as the Tidy Profit's sails fill, and she slides out of the harbour without you. Somewhere up the coast road, the hunters' horses are getting closer.

missed_the_boat.name: The Back Alleys
missed_the_boat.description: At dawn you hear the Tidy Profit's anchor chain rattle up. By noon, the hunters are asking after you at every inn in town.
